title: Embedding schema versioning, client adapter strategy, and phased reindex
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We need a safe, observable way to change the canonical embedding vector dimensionality that minimizes client disruptions, keeps reranking/nearest-neighbor latency stable, and allows per-tenant rollouts. Scope covers API schema, SDK adapters, index on-disk format, and a phased reindex strategy for hosted indexes. Goals: (1) Define a versioned embedding schema that accompanies vectors with metadata, (2) implement backward-compatible SDK adapters that detect and convert between dims when safe, (3) enable dual-write + aliasing reindex flow for zero-downtime migrations, and (4) provide monitoring and automated throttles for reindex worker impact on runtime SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v2 design doc accepted by API and runtime owners
Server accepts and stores schema-versioned vectors with per-vector dim metadata
SDKs (JS/Python) ship adapters that validate dims and support automatic client upgrade path
Reindex tooling supports staggered per-tenant backfills with health gating
No regression >5% in 99th percentile latency for top-100 customers during migration test runs
rollout_plan: Publish schema v2 RFC and get signoff from product/infra/security
Release SDK adapters as opt-in alpha that warn on dim mismatch
Enable server to accept mixed-schema reads by routing to appropriate index alias
Run staged reindex on a small cohort of low-traffic tenants (canary) with telemetry
If canary stable, expand cohort with automated pacing; finally flip default to schema v2 and deprecate v1 after 6 weeks
migration_steps: 1) Define wire schema: {embedding: bytes, dim: int, schema_version: "2", metadata: {model_id: string, quantization: string}}
2) Add per-index aliasing so new index names (index-v2) can be created and switched atomically
3) Implement dual-write option in ingest pipeline to write to both v1 and v2 during migration windows
4) Build reindex worker with rate limit controls and backpressure integration with serving autoscaler
5) Provide reindex-runbook and abort/playback controls in Console for operator visibility
client_changes: SDKs will expose an Adapter layer that: validates embedding length, emits deprecation warnings, and can optionally upcast/pad older vectors when client opts in
New SDK default will be to reject mismatched dims unless client sets 'enable_dim_adapter': true
REST API will return a clear 400 error for incompatible dims with a link to migration docs
Client-side batching behavior updates: SDK will group only same-dim vectors into a single batch request to avoid server-side conversion cost
runtime_changes: Store per-vector dim metadata so indexes can host multiple dims temporarily
Index storage: use compact on-disk representation that tags blocks by dim to avoid per-vector padding overhead
Query planner will select candidate index shards by dim and then merge results, falling back to cross-dim scoring using a lightweight projection if enabled
Autoscaler and reindex worker integration: reindex worker reduces concurrency when serving latency rises above SLOs
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema parsing and validation in server and SDKs
Synthetic load tests: migration simulation with 10K tenants and spike patterns to measure tail latency impact
Staged canary: run on 5 production tenants for 48h, capture token-cost delta, P50/P95/P99 latency, correctness on reranking benchmarks
Chaos test: kill index replicas during reindex to verify alias fallback and failover behavior

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cross-dim scoring could introduce quality regressions. Mitigation: Run offline reranking evals against held-out prompts and compare MRR/NDCG before enabling projection. Default to no cross-dim scoring unless per-tenant opt-in.
Risk: Reindexing floods serving capacity. Mitigation: enforce global and per-tenant rate limits and integrate reindex backpressure with serving autoscaler and maintenance windows in Console.
Risk: SDK auto-conversion hides client bugs. Mitigation: adapters default to opt-in and emit structured telemetry; provide clear migration docs and explicit upgrade path
